sources.title: ‘We Want to Clear Rodrigo’s Name’: Mother of Harvard Student who Died in Bali Says He was Beaten by Police | The Harvard Crimson
sources.claim_summary: The Harvard Crimson (1 September 2022): the mother of Rodrigo Ventocilla, a 32-year-old Peruvian transgender man who co-founded a Lima trans-rights group and studied at the Harvard Kennedy School, alleges he was beaten by police and received inadequate medical care before dying in a Denpasar hospital while still in police custody, days after being arrested for marijuana possession at Bali's airport on his honeymoon; the family alleges extortion demands rising from $100,000 to $200,000, claims the arrest was motivated by racism and transphobia, and says they hold evidence of torture, disputing the official account.

sources.title: Indonesia’s Transgender Community Is Facing Growing Repression – The Diplomat
sources.claim_summary: The Diplomat feature (14 August 2026) on Indonesia's trans community facing growing repression: President Prabowo Subianto's October 2025 presidential decree listed "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among nonmilitary security threats alongside terrorism and drugs; a wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women during 14-16 July 2026, including in West Java's Bogor, followed, as the government moves to codify anti-LGBTQ+ attitudes into law.
